correctness.rationale: PASS. For σ uniform in S_n and q=2^k independent uniformly colored atoms representing k generating subsets, the subalgebra generated by all Boolean operations and iterated forward/backward permutation automorphisms is exactly the partition algebra of equality of two-sided itineraries. Within an ell-cycle, distinct itineraries require a primitive word; between equal-length cycles, their primitive necklaces must be distinct. The conditional number is ∏_ell ell^{c_ell}(L_ell(q))_falling(c_ell) with L_ell(q)=ell^-1∑_{d|ell}μ(d)q^{ell/d}. Averaging over permutation cycle types gives ∏(1+z^ell)^{L_ell(q)}, which follows from the classical Witt product to equal (1-qz²)/(1-qz). Coefficients give n! (q^n-q^{n-1}) generating pairs for n>=2 and n!q for n=1, hence probability 1-2^-k independent of n>=2. My separate direct itinerary enumeration checked five (q,n) pairs including q2 n2..4 and q4 n2..3; the package checker verifies primitive necklaces, all σ≤6 and generating series coefficients. Those finite checks only corroborate the formal all-size proof.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge for the direct tense-Boolean algebra generation interpretation and exact average, with classical Witt, Möbius necklaces and squarefree count explicitly excluded from claimed novelty. Bezhanishvili–Kornell (2025) complete primary text §4 classifies the poset of tense operators by interior relations, not the probability that uniform random generators under a bijective operator generate a full finite algebra. Gessel–Restivo–Reutenauer (2012) studies words/multisets of necklaces and the classical enumerator but not the logical-generation event. The identity is elementary once the itinerary equivalence is discovered, but that conditional census is an independently natural invariant of a standard modal/tense structure. Prior equivalent permutation-coloring enumeration is possible.

The exact all-dimension generation probability and conditional cycle-type census are natural algebraic-generator invariants: the surprising independence from n and use of iterated temporal observations illuminate sampling finite dynamical Boolean models. For finite permutations, past shifts can also be expressed as powers of the forward permutation; no necessity of having both as separate primitives is claimed. This is not an arbitrary numerical coincidence nor a claim that the classical squarefree-polynomial identity is new.
